newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian bank delays foreign ownership decision.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian bank delays foreign ownership decision.

text.p: Slovenian bank Dolenjska banka said on Tuesday it would postpone a decision on whether to open itself to foreign shareholders until a new banking law is passed.

"The managing board proposed to move the decision on whether to enable a 15-percent foreign ownership in the bank from the shareholders meeting until the new banking law is passed," deputy chief executive Milena Dular, told Reuters.

The new law, which will allow international banks to open branches in Slovenia and to buy into local banks in line with EU regulations, is expected to be adopted by parliament later this year, one analyst said.

Last month, Japan's Daiwa Bank said it was interested in buying into Slovenia's eighth largest bank, but that the purchase would first need approval from the Bank of Slovenia. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
